subject: general
question: Which of the following is a microfinance institution of India?

options.text: Small Industries Development Bank of India

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ascend Financial Services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Microfinance institutions do not focus exclusively on urban areas; in fact, they are often focused on rural and underserved areas where financial services are scarce.
 
• Providing loan facilities in rural areas is a more typical goal, not just in urban areas
 
• Microfinance institutions (MFIs) in India are primarily aimed at providing financial services, especially small loans, to individuals and communities who lack access to traditional banking services
 
• MFIs may also offer other financial services, such as: Savings accounts, Insurance, Money transfers, and Energy loans. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• MFIs often provide loans through Joint Lending Groups (JLGs), which are informal groups of 4–10 people who work in similar economic activities and jointly repay loans.
 
• Other types of groups that MFIs may organize include: Self Help Groups (SHGs), Grameen Model Banks, and Rural Cooperatives. 
 
• MFIs can be regulated by the RBI in different ways depending on their type: 
 
 
• Bank-led MFIs: These are subsidiaries of banks and are regulated by the RBI.
 
• NBFC MFIs: These are categorized as Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) and are regulated by the RBI.
 
• Non-profit MFIs: These are typically registered as societies or trusts and operate on a not-for-profit basis.
